title: Emit Dedicated pool readiness SLIs (scheduler health + capacity signal) and wire into SLO dashboards
author: Vanessa Ortiz
description:
Motivation: Dedicated tier needs a first-class readiness SLI that captures the two things customers actually experience during incidents/maintenance windows: (1) whether the pool scheduler is able to accept/route work, and (2) whether there is sufficient allocatable capacity to serve requests without queuing indefinitely. This PR adds canonical readiness signal emission for Dedicated pools and wires the new signals into the existing SLO dashboard set.

What’s included (high-level):
- New metrics emitted from the Dedicated scheduler + capacity manager:
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_scheduler_healthy{region, pool, cluster} (gauge: 0/1)
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_allocatable_gpus{region, pool, cluster} (gauge)
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_allocatable_tokens_per_sec{region, pool, cluster} (gauge; best-effort estimate)
  - redwood_dedicated_pool_ready{region, pool, cluster} (gauge: 0/1; derived)
- Readiness derivation (server-side, single source of truth):
  - pool_ready = scheduler_healthy && allocatable_gpus >= min_gpus_ready && controlplane_connected
  - min_gpus_ready comes from pool config; defaults to 1 for small pools, otherwise ceil(requested_gpus * 0.1) with an upper cap of 8.
  - controlplane_connected uses an existing heartbeat; we’re reusing it but now exposing it via the derived readiness.
- Dashboard integration:
  - Adds a “Dedicated / Pool readiness” row to the standard SLO dashboard template with:
    - Readiness over time (pool_ready)
    - Scheduler health over time
    - Capacity (allocatable_gpus + tokens/sec estimate)
    - “Top pools by unready minutes (24h)” table
  - Adds a link-out to the error budget policy page and the (draft) runbook section for readiness dips.

Notes on scope / safety:
- Dedicated readiness is emitted with tier=dedicated semantics, but we intentionally avoid customer_id labeling here to prevent accidental data leakage and to keep cardinality bounded. Pool label uses the internal pool slug (already access-controlled in dashboards). Customer-specific views can be composed by joining pool->customer mapping in restricted backends (follow-up work).
- This PR does not add paging. SRE policy for readiness is still “ticket-only unless paired with elevated 5xx/latency burn,” per current discussions. We just provide the raw signals so burn-rate alerting can reference them.

Implementation details:
- The scheduler publishes a periodic readiness snapshot (10s) to the metrics emitter. Capacity signal is computed from allocator state (allocatable GPUs) plus a conservative tokens/sec estimate from recent throughput samples (5m EMA) with guardrails when sample volume is low.
- Added unit tests for readiness derivation and for config defaults.

Example metric emission:
- redwood_dedicated_pool_ready{region="us-east-1",pool="ded-7f3a",cluster="gpu-a"} 1
- redwood_dedicated_pool_scheduler_healthy{region="us-east-1",pool="ded-7f3a",cluster="gpu-a"} 1
- redwood_dedicated_pool_allocatable_gpus{region="us-east-1",pool="ded-7f3a",cluster="gpu-a"} 12

Changed areas/files (high-level):
- services/dedicated-scheduler/readiness/readiness.go (new derived readiness + config)
- services/dedicated-scheduler/metrics/emit.go (new gauges + sampling)
- services/capacity-manager/signals/allocatable.go (export allocatable gpu signal)
- config/pools/schema.yaml (min_gpus_ready + validation)
- observability/dashboards/slo/dedicated_pool_readiness.json (new panels + links)
- observability/dashboards/slo/templates/dedicated_slo_overview.json (adds readiness section)
- docs/internal/sre/slo-links.md (dashboard/runbook linkage)

Rollout plan:
- Dark launch metrics behind feature flag dedicated.readiness_metrics_enabled (default off).
- Enable in staging for all pools.
- Enable in prod for 3 pilot pools (per ENG-2419) and validate cardinality + correctness with Nadia.
- After validation, enable for all Dedicated pools.

Testing:
- Unit: readiness derivation, config defaults, allocator signal boundaries.
- Integration: local scheduler + fake allocator; verified metrics endpoint emits expected labels/values.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Alert rules referencing readiness dips paired with burn spikes (ENG-2420).
- Restricted customer-facing readiness aggregation in Console (PM-led workstream).

---
Review conversation (abridged):
- Rafael Mendes: “Can we be explicit about what ‘ready’ means? Right now it looks like a second scheduler health metric.”
  - Vanessa Ortiz: “Added derived definition in code comments + README snippet; ready includes control plane connectivity + capacity threshold.”
- Nadia Rahman: “Please avoid high-cardinality labels (pool_id is okay; do not add model or customer). Also ensure pool label comes from a bounded registry.”
  - Vanessa Ortiz: “Confirmed: labels are region/pool/cluster only. Pool slug comes from config registry; tests added to reject arbitrary pool names.”
- Keiko Yamamoto: “Tokens/sec estimate can be noisy; what happens on cold pools?”
  - Vanessa Ortiz: “We clamp to ‘unknown’ (omit tokens/sec metric) until min samples are present; readiness does not depend on tokens/sec, only allocatable GPUs + scheduler health.”
- Sergio Costa: “Dashboard change looks good; please add a panel that shows unready minutes aggregated per region.”
  - Vanessa Ortiz: “Added ‘unready minutes (24h) by region’ panel + standard filters.”
- Gabe Wilson: “Edge case: allocator reports allocatable GPUs >0 but scheduler is in drain mode.”
  - Vanessa Ortiz: “Drain mode now sets scheduler_healthy=0; readiness follows.”

CI / checks:
- build (monorepo) ✅
- unit tests ✅
- lint ✅
- dashboard validation ✅

Outcome:
- Merged (squash) into main. Feature flag remains OFF by default; enabling tracked in ENG-2419 rollout checklist.
